prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
The offshore wind farm concept covers operation and maintenance for safe, reliable electrical generation, personnel safety, and asset integrity. Operational scope includes wind farm assets, offshore support facilities, control functions, and maintenance activities. Physical boundary begins at turbine structures and includes the turbine array and Offshore Substation. Electrical boundary follows the export connection to the Grid Interface Relay, representing the external-grid interface. Included representative turbine systems: Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Rotor Brake Unit, Turbine Sensor Bus. Other included elements: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, SCADA Gateway, and associated monitoring/control functions. Boundary terminates at defined connections to shore-based control, grid operations, ports, suppliers, and emergency services. Public grid assets beyond the agreed connection point and port operations unrelated to farm logistics are excluded. No aliases or call signs are specified.
Shore Control Room performs continuous monitoring and dispatch coordination. The control interface includes operational coordination with Fleet Dispatch Console and Maintenance Planning Engine; specific item exchanges are not defined.
Lifecycle phases: commissioning/acceptance, routine operation, major refurbishment, eventual decommissioning. Commissioning transitions construction control to operations control through documented handover and verification. Normal-service decisions use validated asset status, approved procedures, current forecasts, and applicable grid instructions. Planned maintenance scheduling considers equipment condition, resource availability, access constraints, and production requirements. Unplanned maintenance uses prioritized fault assessment and controlled mobilization proportional to failure severity. End-of-life activities support safe isolation, removal planning, and transfer of residual operational records to the responsible organization.
Availability objectives use condition monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance, and coordinated offshore access. Safety requires authorized work, controlled hazards, and personnel/vessel accountability throughout operations. Environmental objectives require pollution prevention, minimized marine disturbance, and prompt environmental-incident response.

New part:
S021: Marine coordination covers the Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, and applicable vessel operating procedures.
S022: Workforce interfaces include access management through the North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, and Personnel Tracking Console.
S023: Supply interfaces cover inventory and replenishment coordination through the Warehouse System and Spares Hub.
S024: External interfaces include weather services, metocean observations, grid dispatch, port support, and emergency response organizations.
S025: Cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, and backup power are treated as enabling functions within the farm operations boundary.
S026: This section establishes the operating context and naming convention for the offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system.
S027: The system boundary covers offshore generation assets, supporting marine and shore facilities, operational personnel, and external organizations involved in farm activities.
S028: The farm operates in a variable marine environment where access, equipment condition, and grid requirements influence the timing and conduct of work.
S029: Canonical entity names are used throughout this document to identify system parts, actors, operational states, and controlled items.
S030: In this document, Turbine Controller is referred to by the alias Glassfin.
S031: In this document, Offshore Substation is referred to by the alias Morrowick.
S032: In this document, Weather Service is referred to by the alias Pale Lantern.
S033: The Turbine Controller represents the control function associated with an individual turbine.
S034: Pitch System and Rotor Brake Unit are turbine subsystems considered within the operational boundary.
S035: Converter Cabinet and Nacelle Condition Monitor are treated as distinct turbine equipment for maintenance planning and condition review.
S036: The Blade Inspection Drone is an operational asset used for turbine blade assessment.
S037: The Offshore Substation provides the farm's offshore electrical collection and switching environment.
S038: Main Transformer and Export Cable Monitor are included as substation and export-system assets, respectively.
S039: SCADA Gateway is the supervisory interface associated with farm monitoring and control operations.
S040: Shore Control Room provides a shore-based operating location for authorized personnel.
S041: Fleet Dispatch Console supports the coordination of operational resources across the farm.
S042: Maintenance Planning Engine supports the preparation and sequencing of maintenance activities.
S043: Weather Service represents the external weather information capability considered by farm operations.
S044: Metocean Buoy represents an offshore source of environmental observations within the operating context.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
